name: genuine
how: Signed at capture with a test identity; analysed with that identity's root as a trust anchor.
headline: Valid content credentials, signed by ProvenanceLens Sample Camera (trusted). No forensic evidence of editing.

name: edited
how: A 180x180 patch from another JPEG pasted at (300, 60), then re-exported. No credentials.
headline: Moderate forensic evidence of editing: saved as jpeg more than once; ghost highlights a region.

name: tampered
how: The signed genuine image with a single bit flipped in the compressed pixel data.
headline: Content credentials are present but INVALID: The image bytes changed after signing (hard binding broken): pixels or file structure were modified. Strong forensic evidence of editing: content credentials broken.

name: ai-labelled
how: Credentials declare trainedAlgorithmicMedia. (The pixels are a public-domain photo: what is under test is that a declared label is found and shown, not a guess from pixels.)
headline: Valid content credentials, signed by ProvenanceLens Sample Camera (trusted). AI generation is declared. No forensic evidence of editing.

name: stripped
how: A PNG with no metadata, no credentials and no JPEG history.
headline: No provenance, limited forensic signal: no content credentials, no metadata, and no format-specific statistics to test. Nothing here supports a conclusion either way.
